n: Church of the Holy Archangels Michael and Gabriel
w: Built in the 13th or 14th century, this partially preserved Eastern Orthodox church forms part of the Ancient Nesebar UNESCO World Heritage Site on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. A single-nave design with three apses, it once carried a dome and bell tower and is decorated in Nesebar's distinctive banded stone-and-brick exterior style.
s: A part-ruined Byzantine church on Nesebar's rock
_facts: Medieval Eastern Orthodox church built 13th-14th century
Part of the Ancient Nesebar UNESCO World Heritage Site
Single-nave church with three apses; dome and bell tower now lost

w: Likely raised in the 13th or 14th century, the Church of Saint Paraskevi is one of the partially preserved medieval churches making up the Ancient Nesebar UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has a single nave and an unusual pentagonal apse, richly decorated outside, though its dome and belfry above the narthex have both been lost, and no one is sure which of three saints named Paraskevi it honours.
s: Nesebar church, dedicated to an uncertain Paraskevi
_facts: Medieval Eastern Orthodox church, likely 13th-14th century
Single nave with a pentagonal apse
Dedication among three saints named Paraskevi is unresolved

w: Built in the 13th century, the Church of St Theodore keeps its original north and west facades, though later builders replaced the other walls and roof. The single-nave church, just 8.7 metres long and 4.15 metres wide, wears Nesebar's signature decoration: blind stone arches filled with staggered zigzag patterns of stone and brick.
s: Zigzag brick and stone on a tiny 13th-century church
_facts: Built in the 13th century; north and west facades original
Single nave with narthex and apse, 8.70m by 4.15m
Facade decorated with blind arches and zigzag brick-and-stone patterns

w: Raised in 1609 within the UNESCO-listed old town of Nesebar, the Church of the Holy Saviour is a small single-nave building, just 11.7 by 5.7 metres, notable for wall paintings from its earliest years depicting scenes from the life of Christ and the Virgin. Long deconsecrated, it now doubles as a museum; the tombstone of Byzantine princess Mataissa Cantacuzina, once kept here, has since moved to Nesebar's archaeological museum.
s: Nesebar church turned museum, minus its royal tomb
